question.text: Which of the following is a unique benefit of Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGBs) compared to physical gold and gold ETFs?

answer.text: SGBs provide exposure to international gold prices
SGBs pay 2.5% per annum interest semi-annually in addition to gold price appreciation
SGBs can be redeemed at any time without restriction
SGBs are exempt from GST like physical gold

explanation.text: The Logic: Per NISM Series X-B, SGBs uniquely pay 2.50% per annum interest, credited semi-annually, in addition to any price appreciation linked to gold. Physical gold, gold funds, and gold ETFs do not generate any periodic income. SGBs also avoid GST cost, eliminate purity and storage concerns, and allow RBI redemption between 5 and 8 years. The Trap: The "exempt from GST like physical gold" option is doubly wrong because physical gold attracts GST cost while SGBs do not, so the comparison is reversed. SGBs also cannot be redeemed at any time without restriction; they have a defined RBI redemption window after 5 to 8 years. Note: The exact statutory GST rate on physical gold is not stated on the checked NISM source pages, so quote only the qualitative point that physical gold incurs a GST cost and SGBs do not, unless a current tax source is cited.
